title: standardize-dataset-license-and-profile-metadata-harmonizer
author: Nina Park
commits_summary: 7 commits: introduce canonical license field, add migration script and dry-run mode, extend profile schema, add changelog delta emitter for license/metadata changes, tests and docs
description:
Motivation: model profiles currently carry free-form dataset_licenses and provenance text which leads to inconsistent UX in the Console and noisy release notes when onboarding models. This PR introduces a canonical dataset license field (dataset_license.canonical) plus a harmonizer/migration tool that standardizes legacy licenses into SPDX-like tags and emits concise changelog deltas for automated release notes.

Summary of changes: added a new optional top-level `dataset_license` block to model_profile schema (name, canonical, source_url, declared_by). Implemented `scripts/migrate_licenses.py` which runs a best-effort mapping table and a dry-run mode that outputs normalization suggestions. Added `tooling/changelog/emit_license_delta.py` to produce machine-readable delta snippets consumed by the release assembler. Adjusted onboarding hook to record `license_normalization_hint` in the onboard logs when mapping was ambiguous. Updated tests, examples, and docs.

Backward compatibility & rollout: the schema change is additive and backward compatible; existing profiles without the new block are unaffected. The migration script is opt-in and has a dry-run mode by default; after review we executed the non-destructive migration for models in the staging bucket and pushed suggested canonicalizations as PRs to the registry metadata. The Console will prefer `dataset_license.canonical` if present, falling back to legacy free-form text.

Checklist: [x] schema extension and migration tool added; [x] unit + integration tests; [x] changelog emitter integrated with release assembler hook; [x] docs/Console mapping notes; [x] Linear linked.

How to test locally: run `python scripts/migrate_licenses.py --dry-run --input examples/profiles/` to see normalization suggestions. To apply changes to a writable registry, run with `--apply` and review the generated commit. Use `python tooling/changelog/emit_license_delta.py --from old.json --to new.json` to preview the release fragment.

Rollback: migration changes are committed as separate commits per profile and are reversible via the generated revert commits in the output repo; the emitters are read-only until release assembler consumes them.

Related: ENG-7421 (standardize metadata for legal/compliance), SUP-1987 (support ticket: ambiguous dataset licenses encountered during onboarding).
